message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me go through it step by step. First, I was renting a place with this dude, and we were on a lease. When the lease was ending, he just left without giving much notice. He took most of his stuff, leaving only the last bit of his half of the rent and a few things he didn't want to bring with him. He left a note saying he didn't want those things. Now, where I live, if you don't get rid of your stuff when you move out, the landlord can pay someone to remove it, and that cost comes out of your deposit. I've heard of people losing $250 because of this. So, I tried to contact him for two weeks, texting and emailing, asking him to pick up his stuff or let me take them to the dump. He never responded. So, I took most of his stuff to the dump, but he had around 60 video games for the PS4. I thought, why not sell them? There's a local game store that buys used games, and they gave me $600 for all of his games. That's a decent amount of money. Then, last week, I saw him at a party. We were being polite, and he asked how the move-out went. I said it was good, and he asked what I did with his stuff. When he found out I sold his games, he got mad. I told him I tried to reach out to him, but he never responded. Now he's calling me an asshole and asking for the money back. I checked legally, and there's nothing I did wrong. But now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for selling his games. Hmm, so the main points are: he left without taking his stuff, I tried to contact him, he didn't respond, I took his stuff to the dump, sold the games for $600, and now he's upset. I think legally, I'm in the clear because I tried to contact him, and the landlord would have charged him if I didn't do anything. But morally, is it right to sell someone's stuff without their permission, even if they left it behind? On one hand, I saved him from potentially losing money from his deposit. On the other hand, I took his property and sold it without his consent. Even though he left it, maybe I should have handled it differently, like donating the games or giving them to someone else instead of selling them for profit. I also wonder if the $600 is a lot of money for him. Maybe he didn't realize how many games he had or their value. Selling them without his knowledge might have been a bit underhanded, even if I had good intentions to prevent him from losing money. So, maybe I should have found another way to dispose of his stuff without selling it. Or, if I did sell them, perhaps I should have given him the money or at least discussed it with him first. But since he didn't respond, I didn't have a choice. I'm still not sure. Legally, I'm fine, but morally, it's a bit gray. I might have crossed a line by selling his property without his consent, even if it was to prevent a bigger loss. Maybe I should have been more considerate of his ownership, even if he abandoned the items.
